sections.title: Basic Concept of Trigonometry
sections.content: Trigonometry is the study of relationships between angles and sides of triangles. Mainly, in right-angled triangles, sine (sin), cosine (cos), and tangent (tan) are used.

sections.title: Simple Examples with Sides and Angles
sections.content: For example, consider a ladder of length 100 units at an angle of 30 degrees with the ground. Using sin, cos, tan, we can calculate the height and base.

sections.title: Formulas for Sin, Cos, and Tan
sections.content: sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite / adjacent

sections.title: Important Trigonometric Identities
sections.content:
1. sin^2θ + cos^2θ = 1
2. 1 + tan^2θ = sec^2θ
3. 1 + cot^2θ = csc^2θ

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Confusing degrees and radians
2. Taking wrong sides for ratio
3. Forgetting the formulas

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In right-angled triangles, remember sin, cos, tan. For small angles, half-angle formulas can help in quick calculations.

tricks.title: Quick 5% method
tricks.explanation: Find 10% first and then take half of it.

tricks.title: Quick increase/decrease
tricks.explanation: For x% increase: new value = original * (1 + x/100), for decrease use (1 - x/100).
